doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: To the US and the Caribbean with Carmen and Rolando
title: Touring Santo Domingo under Trujillo
summary: Six months touring Dominican theaters with Lopez Balaguer, Angel Viloria's conjunto and others; the people were warm to him.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Which towns did you visit?

Well, the towns that I remember right now are naturally the capital, at the Hotel Jaragua. Then we went to Santiago de los Caballeros, Puerto Plata, La Romana, San Pedro Macorí, San Francisco Marcorí, Monte Christi, Moca, Bonao, those are the ones I remember
(Laughs).
How much time in total were you in Santo Domingo?
Another six months.
Another six months.
Aha.
Tell us, you were there at the time of Trujillo, Trujillo's dictatorship. Tell us what impressions did you have and how were you received by the Dominican people.

Very warm. Always looking back over my life in music, as always, that's what I've always tried to be - about the music, nothing more than the music. But they are a very warm people, they admired and respected me a lot. And everywhere they yelled, "Candido, Candido, Candido, Candido."
With whom else did you perform there in Santo Domingo?

Well, the singer Lopez Balaguer took us. And in that same show was Angel Viloria’s Conjunto. There was a singer named Canelina who did Afro-Cuban singing and the dancing couple and me. That was the show. We toured the entire republic with that show.
So then there was Balaguer who was a bolero singer, Angel Viloria . . .
With his group . . .
With his group, Conjunto Tipico Cibaeño.
Exactly.
Was Dioris Valladares the singer at that time?
Yes Yes Yes Yes.
And your show?
Aha.
That was mostly Cuban music.
Exactly.
That is, a bit of everything.
A bit of everything. So everybody was pleased. We did all the theaters - only theaters throughout the republic.
Exactly. Tell me about some of these places - the theaters, radio, television, where you performed.
Well, the first was at the Hotel Jaragua and then the theaters in those towns that I mentioned earlier. There in the main theaters of these towns.
And on the radio?

No, we did not do radio, but we would go often to hear the orchestras . . . in Bonao . . . a radio station . . . I think it was called at that time La Voz del Yuna (The Voice of Yuna). And that was in Bonao. We went there because I believe the drummer of one of the orchestras was Cuban and he would always tell me, "Come to hear the orchestra." And they invited me there for lunch or dinner and stuff. I had a really good time there.
